_comment: Starter guided tour. Replace every step. A target may name a view-spec field ({'attr': 'x'}) or section ({'title': 'Settings'}), a toolbar action ({'action': 'Run'}), a widget objectName ({'name': 'toolAction_run'}), a dock tab ({'tab': 'Results'}) or a navigation-shell row ({'panel': 'Step 1'}). An empty target centres the bubble, which is right for an opening and a closing step and wrong everywhere else. WALK THE TOUR HEADLESSLY once it is written: an unresolvable target does not fail, it silently shows centred, and the tour becomes the slideshow it exists not to be. Format: chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: What this tool is for
steps.text:
One paragraph on what the tool measures and why someone would open it, then say how many steps the tour has so nobody wonders whether to start it.

Replace this.

steps.title: The first thing to press
steps.text:
This is the step the whole format exists for: a help page can say what every control means and still leave someone with no idea which one comes first.

Point at the real control and wait for the user to press it. Never press it for them — someone who watched a button being pressed has not learned where it is.

target.action: Replace with a real toolbar action

steps.title: The setting that decides the answer
steps.text: Pick the control that most changes the result and say what goes wrong when it is wrong — especially if it goes wrong silently. That is the sentence people remember.

steps.title: How to tell whether to believe it
steps.text:
Close on the checks, in the order that catches the most. If the tool can generate its own demo with a known answer, this is where to say so — checking against a known answer is the only thing that turns a plausible result into a trusted one.

The ? button has the long version.
